text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- Wednesday's talks between the Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and Bosnian Alija Izetbegovic will focus on the future use of Croatia's southern Adriatic port of Ploce among other issues.

- Editorial: Interview given by Alija Izetbegovic to weekly Tjednik last week is of extreme importance to the defence of Bosnian Croat General Tihomir Blaskic, tried in The Hague. Izetbegovic at one point makes a comment that contradicts charges of the war crimes tribunal.
- Half a million foreign tourists arrived in Croatia over the weekend.

- Commentary: Croatian Archbishop Alojzije Stepinac, who was tried and sentenced by communist Yugoslavia for allegedly collaborating with Croatian pro-Nazi regime in World War Two, was in fact a resolute fighter against fascism who saved many from persecution. He was not a British Intelligence Service agent, as one weekly recently suggested.
- Some 4.8 percent of all Croatians are on the dole but the figure is on a constant decline.
- State electricity board (HEP) is hurriedly moving mobile diesel electric plants from Dalmatia to Eastern Slavonia to prevent the region from being connected to the Serbian electricity grid.
- Money market: The July average lending rate dropped below 11 percent for the first time in six months. At 10.19 percent it was the lowest since December 1996. Supply of kuna remains quite good.
- Insurance news:
* Sunce Osiguranje expects to see a quick increase of its life insurance portfolio. Its gross premium reached 1.97 million kuna in only two months of active work.
* Osiguranje Aurum d.d. recorded a strong growth of gross premium to 10.57 million kuna in the first half of 1997. In 1996, Aurum's premium income totalled 14.1 million.
- Banking news: Peaceful change at the helm of Dalmatinska Banka -- new board president is Zdravko Bubalo, representative of the bank's biggest shareholder, Croatian emigree Steve Bubalo.
VECERNJI LIST
- Wheat harvest completed with the crop totalling 800,000 tonnes. Autumn wheat sowings to be increased to 280,000 hectares.
- Many tourists arriving in Dubrovnik find no vacancy in any of the hotels or private rooms.
- Bosnia: some 92 political parties, eight coalitions and 155 independent candidates will take part in the municipal race.
- Harassment of Croats continues in the Serbian town of Zemun where radicals, led by Vojislav Seselj, have a majority in the municipal authorities.

- Tennis: In order to enable 15-year-old Mirjana Lucic to play in next season's senior Grand Slam finals, her ambitious father Marinko organised a $500,000 tournament -- International Ladies Championship, which she won on Sunday. Mirjana Lucic is the world's number one junior in women's tennis.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- Franjo Tudjman will be sworn as president in St. Mark's Square in Zagreb on Tuesday.
- Two years after Croatian forces regained control over Knin, it is still perceived as a symbol of the Croatian freedom rather than a town desperately needing help. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
